items.title: AI satellite spots cruise ship and autonomously orders second look
points: Irish space technology company Ubotica has demonstrated a satellite capable of identifying a vessel and independently scheduling a follow-up observation without instructions from ground controllers.

The breakthrough, which the company claims is a world first for commercial Earth observation, could have significant implications for monitoring shadow fleets, dark vessels and threats to subsea infrastructure.
During a demonstration in October, Ubotica’s CogniSAT-6 satellite captured an image of a cruise ship in the Pacific Ocean and used onboard artificial intelligence to identify its location.
The satellite then calculated when it could revisit the same location, automatically scheduling another image two days later.
The second observation confirmed the vessel had departed, with the entire process conducted without ground intervention.
The 6U CubeSat, built and operated by Open Cosmos, was launched aboard a SpaceX rocket in March 2024.
“Autonomous scheduling is about giving satellites the ability to interpret what they see and decide what to do next,” said Ubotica’s director of space system engineering, David Rijlaarsdam.

points: French shipowner LD Armateurs (LDA) has acquired three platform supply vessels currently under construction for conversion into cable-laying ships as it looks to expand its presence in the subsea telecommunications market.
The three vessels are scheduled for delivery in the second quarter of 2027 before heading to an undisclosed shipyard for conversion.
They are expected to enter service in the first quarter of 2028.
Each vessel will have a cable-carrying capacity of 2,800 tonnes and will be equipped for subsea cable installation, maintenance, and repair operations.

The French company, which has more than 25 years of experience in subsea telecommunications cable operations, said the investment would help address growing demand for cable installation and repair capacity amid concerns about an ageing global fleet.

The company has previous experience converting offshore vessels for cable operations, including the Ile de Molène, which entered service with Alcatel Submarine Networks in 2022 following an extensive conversion programme.

items.title: SLB OneSubsea picks up subsea deal for Aker BP’s North Sea project
points: SLB’s OneSubsea joint venture has secured a contract from Aker BP to supply subsea production systems, umbilicals, and associated services for the Lyra oilfield development in the Norwegian North Sea.
The contract, whose value was not disclosed, will support the fast-track development of Lyra, previously known as Kjøttkake, approximately 44 km from the Gjøa platform.
The project comprises three multilateral subsea wells targeting approximately 37m barrels of oil equivalent in recoverable resources, with gross plateau production estimated at around 20,000 boepd.
The development partners are targeting first oil in the first half of 2028, roughly three years after the discovery was made in March 2025.
OneSubsea said it had worked with Aker BP from the early stages of the project to develop a standardised subsea solution aimed at reducing costs and shortening the execution schedule.

The award follows a separate contract worth between $150m and $300m secured earlier this week by Subsea 7 for engineering, procurement, construction, and installation of gas-lift and production pipelines and associated subsea infrastructure.

The agreement covers offshore geotechnical data acquisition using drilling vessels and specialist seabed cone penetration testing vessels, along with laboratory analysis at Fugro facilities in Germany, Belgium, and the UK.
Fugro’s marine operations in Germany and the Netherlands will coordinate the work, with the offshore survey programme scheduled to begin in mid-March 2027.
The framework allows BSH to call off services from the award date.
Fugro did not disclose the agreement’s value or the volume of work expected over its duration.

The investigations will provide seabed and subsurface data for areas earmarked for future offshore wind development, helping prospective developers assess foundation conditions, geological risks and construction requirements before participating in project…

Erik Vogt, project director at Fugro Germany, said the company’s ability to deploy dedicated geotechnical drilling vessels and specialist CPT assets had been an important factor in securing the agreement.
